_meta.title: LIRIL dev-team PASS-rate measurement — 2026-04-18 (3-burn honest record)
_meta.purpose: Three consecutive 10-cycle burns measuring whether the LIRIL self-improvement loop (memory, few-shot, target-file injection, URL gates) actually moves the PASS rate. Honest record including the regression and the noise observation.

baseline.description: Pre-everything, after NATS port fix only

burn_1.description: After fallback parser + URL HEAD-check gate + memory + few-shot (engineer+researcher+gatekeeper)

burn_2.description: After adding verbose citation rules + verified URL bank (LIRIL options C+D+E)
burn_2.interpretation: Regression. Prompt bloat pushed the model into short/empty outputs.

burn_3.description: After reverting URL bloat — kept target-file injection, few-shot, memory
burn_3.interpretation: Did NOT recover the 50% burn-1 number as expected. Three possible reads: (a) burn 1 was a high draw on model variance and the real rate is ~30-35%; (b) target-file injection is net neutral/negative on average; (c) the removed URL-bank/citation-rules were actually net positive for some tasks, and my revert threw away a real gain. 10-cycle samples have insufficient statistical power to distinguish these.

honest_conclusion.measured_fact: Three 10-cycle burns produced 5/10, 3/10, 3/10 PASS. Mean = 3.67/10 = 36.7%. Variance is large on 10-cycle samples, so individual burn-to-burn deltas are mostly noise.
what_is_proven: The pipeline functions: autonomous commits land every burn.
The URL HEAD-check gate catches real hallucinations at the output level (CBC, CHD, tenet5.pvsnp.telemetry examples) — no false positives observed.
The fallback verdict parser converts previously-UNPARSED gatekeeper outputs into valid PASS/WATCH/FAIL verdicts when the content is present.
WS-030 (vaccine-injury reader_guidance) moved from consistent UNPARSED (burn 1, 2) to PASS after target-file injection was added (burn 3). Some tasks genuinely improved with the additional context.
what_is_NOT_proven: That the aggregate PASS rate moved meaningfully from ~33% baseline to ~50%. The sample size and model stochasticity make small deltas undetectable.
That any single prompt-level intervention (few-shot, target-file injection, citation rules) dominates the others.
That further prompt engineering on this 12B Mistral-Nemo model has headroom. It may have hit its quality ceiling for the autonomous dev-team task class.
next_step_candidates: Larger sample (30-50 cycles per burn) to actually resolve +/- 5pp differences.
Different model (Mistral-Nemo 12B is the bottleneck — a larger or fine-tuned model may lift the ceiling).
Output-level gates only (URL HEAD-check, placeholder-text rejection) rather than further prompt additions.
Task decomposition (split complex tasks into atomic subtasks that small models handle better).

cumulative_autonomous_commits_this_sessi: approx 25 across 3 burns + persistent daemon cycles
